title.narrative: Mainstreaming an Integrated Water Resources Management Approach for more Resilient Basins in Mozambique

description.narrative: IUCN in collaboration with the Government of Mozambique Water Resources Management Directorate (DNGARH) will implement an Integrated Water Management Resources Programme, MozWater: 2024-2027, for Mozambique. The MozWater Project will work in Mozambique to achieve water security through effective integrated water resources management in key basins and at a national level. It is a collaborative effort where joint action on the ground will produce key lessons and best practices that inform policy to strengthen business approaches, institutions, and rules around the sustainable use of land and water. MozWater will be implemented collaboratively with Administração Regional Águas do Norte (ARA Norte), Administração Regional de Águas do Centro (ARA Centro) and the National Directorate for Water Resources Management (DNGRH) as primary implementing partners. While other partners may be invited to deliver specific outputs, based on their thematic expertise and local impact and following the project design phase. It is envisaged that the National Disaster Management Institute (INGD) and National Meteorology Institute (INAM) will play important roles.

The focus for the project is to continue and scale up the previous programme, focusing on improved collaboration and stakeholders and investors synergies, access to safe water and to water for economic activities. The aggregated output to this programme will be increased climate resilience and improved sustainable livelihoods, including the promotion of alternative income generating activities and knowledge to plan and adapt in accordance with the landscapes´ evolution.
